'''Paul Woodrow Palmer''' (born October 14, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[Detroit Lions]] and [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He also was a member of the [[Barcelona Dragons (NFL Europe)|Barcelona Dragons]] in the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF). He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple Owls football|Temple Owls]].

==Early life==
Palmer attended [[Winston Churchill High School (Montgomery County, Maryland)|Churchill High School]] in [[Potomac, Maryland]]. He was a versatile [[running back]] and led the state in kickoff returns as a senior.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Simms |first1=Brandy L. |title=Boo-Boo Palmer to be enshrined in college football's Hall of Fame |url=https://mont.thesentinel.com/2018/01/11/boo-boo-palmer-to-be-enshrined-in-college-football-s-hall-of-fame/ |work=Montgomery County Sentinel |date=January 11, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2020 |archive-date=January 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115213159/https://mont.thesentinel.com/2018/01/11/boo-boo-palmer-to-be-enshrined-in-college-football-s-hall-of-fame/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Paul accepted a football scholarship from [[Temple University]], to play under head coach [[Bruce Arians]]. As a freshman he was a backup that struggled with ball security. He registered 141 carries for 628 yards (4.5-yard average), 6 rushing [[touchdown]]s, 33 receptions for 271 yards and 2 [[touchdown]]s.<ref name=inquirer-2018>{{cite news |last1=Narducci |first1=Marc |title=Toughness led Temple's Paul Palmer to the College Football Hall of Fame |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/temple/temple-football-paul-palmer-college-football-hall-of-fame-20181202.html |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=December 2, 2018}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Palmer replaced the injured starter Brian Slade at [[running back]] against [[Boston College]], making 11 carries for 98 yards. The next game against the [[University of Cincinnati]], he registered 92 rushing yards. His first start came against the [[University of Delaware]], collecting 144 rushing yards. He posted 182 carries for 885 yards (4.9/yard average), 9 [[touchdown]]s, 29 receptions for 197 yards and one [[touchdown]].

As a junior, he became one of the top [[running back]]s in the nation, recording 275 carries for 1,516 yards, 9 [[touchdown]]s, 13 receptions for 131 yards and one [[touchdown]]. Against [[Penn State]], he rushed for 206 yards.

As a senior in 1986, Palmer led the [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] in rushing yards (1,866) and all-purpose yards (2,633), breaking [[Marcus Allen]]'s single-season all-purpose yardage [[NCAA]] record. He also registered 346 carries and 15 [[touchdown]]s. Against [[East Carolina University]], he tallied 349 rushing yards (school record), 3 [[touchdown]]s and tied the single-game record for all-purpose yards with 417. In his next three games he rushed for 239, 187, and 212 yards respectively, setting [[NCAA]] records for rushing yards in consecutive games, three straight contests and four consecutive games. Paul was the runner-up to [[Vinny Testaverde]] for the 1986 [[Heisman Trophy]] award, even though Temple did not have nationally televised games.

In July 1988, it emerged that Palmer had signed with agent Norby Walters before his eligibility expired (he received monthly payments and a $5,000 loan). Temple forfeited all six of its wins from the 1986 season, erased all of Palmer's records from the books, and withdrew all of Palmer's athletic prizes and rewards. School president [[Peter Liacouras]] also ordered Palmer to reimburse Temple for his senior year scholarship. In a deal with federal prosecutors who were investigating Walters, Palmer agreed to perform 150 to 250 hours of community service.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sports People; Forfeits by Temple | work=The New York Times | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/07/28/sports/sports-people-forfeits-by-temple.html | access-date=June 12, 2018 | date=July 28, 1988}}</ref> Years later, the school decided to recognize Palmer’s 1986 season, after he showed remorse for his decisions and their effects on Temple.

During Palmers college career he ranked sixth in [[NCAA Division I]] history in rushing yards and fourth in all-purpose yards, setting 23 school records including career rushing yards (4,895), career rushing attempts (944), career all-purpose yards (6,613), career rushing touchdowns (39), career 100-yard games (21), career 200-yard games (6) and points (264).<ref>{{cite news|last1=Missanelli|first1=M.G.|title=Temple Offers To Forfeit 1986 Victories|url=http://articles.philly.com/1988-07-26/sports/26236878_1_owls-football-victories-paul-palmer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130206103512/http://articles.philly.com/1988-07-26/sports/26236878_1_owls-football-victories-paul-palmer|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 6, 2013|access-date=12 September 2015|agency=Philadelphia Media Network (Digital), LLC|date=July 26, 1988}}</ref>

In 2000, Palmer was inducted into the Temple Athletics Hall of Fame. On January 8, 2018, he was elected to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]], becoming the first player from Temple to receive such an honor.<ref name=inquirer-2018/><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/charles-woodson-mack-brown-headline-2018-college-football-hall-of-fame-class/ | title=Charles Woodson, Mack Brown headline 2018 College Football Hall of Fame class | date=8 January 2018 | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Palmer was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the first round (19th overall) of the [[1987 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-25 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His great-grandmother Frances Palmer who raised him since he was 2 years old, died the day he was drafted and Paul chose to spend the day with his family. As a rookie, Palmer was mostly used on [[special teams]], leading the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] in kickoff return average (24.3 yards per attempt). He was named to the [[NFL]]'s All-Rookie Team, and was named NFL All-Pro as a kick returner.

In [[1988 NFL season|1988]], through the first six weeks Paul led the team in rushing, receiving, scoring and combined yards from scrimmage. He would later have clashes with the coaching staff and not be able to take over the starting [[running back]] position from [[Christian Okoye]]. On September 4, [[1989 NFL season|1989]], Palmer was waived by new head coach [[Marty Schottenheimer]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1310&dat=19890905&id=HvNVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=y-EDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6330,1290585&hl=es | title=Transactions | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref> He rushed for 607 yards in two seasons.

===Detroit Lions===
On September 5, [[1989 NFL season|1989]], Palmer was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Lions]], reuniting with [[Frank Gansz]] who was his head coach with the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=19890906&id=Z0RPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=AAMEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3864,5273695&hl=es | title=Transactions | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref> On October 16, after five games without a single rushing attempt and 11 kickoff returns for 255 yards, he was traded to the [[Dallas Cowboys]], in exchange for an eighth round draft choice (#194-[[Willie Green (American football)|Willie Green]]).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1989-10-17-sp-261-story.html | title=Dallas Sends Pelluer to Chiefs, Picks Up Palmer From Lions | website=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=17 October 1989 | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
In [[1989 NFL season|1989]], he became the starting [[running back]] after [[Herschel Walker]] was traded to the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. Palmer led the Cowboys with 446 yards on 112 carries during 9 games, on a team that would finish with a 1–15 record for the [[1989 NFL season|1989 season]], and that had the second lowest 16-game rushing total in franchise history (after the [[2012 NFL season|2012 season]]), with [[quarterback]] [[Troy Aikman]] as the team's second-leading rusher with 302 yards. Palmer played a key role in the only win the team had that season (against Washington), when Paul registered the only 100-yard rushing game of his career, after gaining 110 yards and scoring a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1989-11-06-sp-624-story.html | title=Finally, Cowboys Get a Victory : Dallas: Return of Redskin quarterback Doug Williams is spoiled | website=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=6 November 1989 | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On March 30, [[1990 NFL season|1990]], the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] signed him in [[Plan B free agency]]. Palmer led the team in kickoff return yardage during the preseason (5 kick returns for an average of 23 yards, including a 49-yarder against Atlanta). He was released on August 20.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://articles.philly.com/1990-08-22/sports/25934071_1_bengals-special-teams-bengals-coach-sam-wyche-paul-palmer | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202832/http://articles.philly.com/1990-08-22/sports/25934071_1_bengals-special-teams-bengals-coach-sam-wyche-paul-palmer | url-status=dead | archive-date=October 29, 2013 | title=Paul Palmer Is Released By Bengals | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Barcelona Dragons (first stint)===
In [[1991 WLAF season|1991]], he was drafted by the [[Barcelona Dragons (NFL Europe)|Barcelona Dragons]] of the [[World League of American Football]]. During the first 4 games Palmer was the league's second leading rusher, but a hamstring injury limited him to just 39 yards the rest of the season. He finished as the team's second leading-rusher behind Jim Bell, recording 358 yards and 3 [[touchdown]]s.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1734&dat=19910408&id=elccAAAAIBAJ&sjid=a1IEAAAAIBAJ&pg=2412,5147363&hl=es | title=Paul Palmer Gets Another Chance With New League | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On June 27, [[1991 NFL season|1991]], Paul was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19910628&id=Tk4yAAAAIBAJ&sjid=YuYFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2819,3739034&hl=es | title=Eagles sign former Chief | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref> He was released on August 5.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1955&dat=19910806&id=xYU0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=96IFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2447,2784891&hl=es | title=Birds Waive Paul Palmer | access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Barcelona Dragons (second stint)===
In [[1992 WLAF season|1992]], Palmer finished his professional career in the [[World League of American Football]] with the [[Barcelona Dragons (NFL Europe)|Barcelona Dragons]]. He was the Dragons starting running back, tallying 259 total rushing yards.

==Personal life==
Palmer spent 12 seasons as an assistant football coach at [[Haddon Heights High School]]. He is currently a radio analyst for Temple football games.
